answer: On a karst coast, AI agents trading wharf capacity must lock $100 of collateral per account to submit at most ten bids daily. The bond stays locked for a 30-day horizon after the last bid, so an attacker cannot recycle one deposit through fresh identities. Running 1,000 fake agents therefore requires $100,000 tied up for at least a month: identities remain cheap to create, but multiplying their bidding power is not.
